title: WP-CLI Configuration Schema
description: JSON Schema for validating wp-cli.yml configuration files

ssh.description: Perform operation against a remote server over SSH (or a container using scheme of "docker", "docker-compose", "docker-compose-run", "vagrant").

http.description: Perform operation against a remote WordPress installation over HTTP.

url.description: Pretend request came from given URL. In multisite, this argument is how the target site is specified.

skip-plugins.description: Skip loading all or some plugins. Note: mu-plugins are still loaded.

skip-themes.description: Skip loading all or some themes.

require.description: Load PHP file before running the command (may be used more than once).

exec.description: Execute PHP code before running the command (may be used more than once).

trust-project-config.description: Trust the project-level wp-cli.yml (or wp-cli.local.yml) file so that the require, exec, env, ssh-args and connection (ssh, http, ssh_config, proxyjump, key) settings and the aliases it introduces are acted upon. Accepts true, false, or a path (or list of paths) to a trusted wp-cli.yml file or project directory; relative paths are resolved against the configuration file that lists them. Only honored in the system and global configuration files, where the global value takes precedence over the system one; a project configuration cannot grant itself trust. Precedence overall: the --trust-project-config parameter, then the global and system config files, then the trust store (trusted-configs.json next to the global config file, written when answering 'a' at the prompt), then the WP_CLI_TRUST_PROJECT_CONFIG environment variable, then an interactive prompt. Without a TTY an undecided project config is an error, so in CI prefer a path over true.

oneOf.description: Path to a trusted project directory or wp-cli.yml file

items.description: Path to a trusted project directory or wp-cli.yml file

context.description: Load WordPress in a given context.

oneOf.description: A context that simulates running a command as if it would be executed in the administration backend.
Switches between 'cli' and 'admin' depending on which command is being used.
This is something in-between a frontend and an admin request, to get around some of the quirks of WordPress when running on the console.

debug.description: Show all PHP errors; add verbosity to WP-CLI bootstrap.

apache_modules.description: List of Apache Modules that are to be reported as loaded.

env.description: Set environment variable values. These will be used as fallbacks when the corresponding environment variable is not set in the shell. All values are converted to strings.

merge.description: Merge subcommand defaults from the upstream config.yml, instead of overriding

inherit.description: Inherit configuration from an arbitrary YAML file

_.description: '_' is a special value denoting configuration options for this wp-cli.yml

url.description: Pretend request came from given URL. In multisite, this argument is how the target site is specified.

ssh.description: Perform operation against a remote server over SSH (or a container using scheme of "docker", "docker-compose", "docker-compose-run", "vagrant").

http.description: Perform operation against a remote WordPress installation over HTTP.

oneOf.description: Aliases can reference other aliases to create alias groups. Alias groups can be nested

^@[_a-zA-Z][_a-zA-Z0-9]*$.description: Aliases to other WordPress installs (e.g. `wp @staging rewrite flush`)
